Annual event during which the centre of Madrid is free of cars and is instead filled with shepherds exercising their ancient right to drive sheep and livestock through the city.

Annual event held between the last week of June and the first of July, with more than 1.5 million people in the street from all around the world. It began as a weekend party, but lately turned into a full-week extravaganza.

Performs every Th and F at the Teatro Monumental on Calle Atocha.
Probably the best known V.O. (versión original, or original language) theatre in Madrid, it offers the largest selection of movies and is a short walk from Sol.

This is a wonderful old Spanish theatre dating from the 1920s. It has three screens and shows mainly art-house and critically acclaimed films in the original language. In the summertime, they screen movies on the roof.
An authentic flamenco show in the heart of Madrid, set in a traditional exposed brick cave of the XIX century. Daily shows at 18:00, 19:30 and 21:00. Free drink included.

This museum is dedicated to the history of Madrid from 1561 to present. Much of the history is explained by referencing exhibited paintings depicting people or events from the time, so it is also an art museum. Several maps and models…

see.n: Plaza de Toros de Las Ventas

Eye-catching twin towers, constructed 1967–74. With 116 metres and height and 23 floors, they are among the highest buildings in Madrid.
Circular place and nice green space (thanks to the motorised traffic being directed through a tunnel), surrounded by an ensemble of colourful 19th-century residential buildings.

Modern circular building from the early 1980s, designed by architects Bonet and Valdés.

This cinema is located in a shopping mall known for its ice-skating rink. It is a great place where teenagers can hang out since the mall also has restaurants, bars, and shops.
Imposing and highly ornamental Art nouveau (or modernismo) building at the western corner of Plaza de España, designed by Federico Arias Rey and completed in 1914.
Francoist triumph arch erected 1950–56 to commemorate the Nationalist victory in the Battle of Ciudad Universitaria of the Civil War.

see.b: This small church is famous for its murals, painted by Goya. It's also the mausoleum of the painter.

The rose garden of Madrid, located in the same park as the Templo de Debod. If you like roses and are in Madrid when they have flowered, definitely worth a visit. The garden holds an international competition yearly.

The park at the rear of the Palacio Real which used to belong to the Royal family. Much of the park has been taken to smaller activity parks such as the Zoo but in general it's peaceful. From Moncloa you can take a teleferico (€5.90…

see.b: See the pandas, pet the lemurs, watch the dolphin show, and enjoy the bird show.

A very popular flamenco tablao located near the Plaza España metro station. The package consisting of a Flamenco show (at 21:00 or 22:00) with a candle-lit dinner and a glass of Sangria wine is truly a treat.
National touring acts for rock and pop music.

Tapas restaurant
Tapas restaurant
Mid-range Mexican restaurant with an extensive range of authentic options, though do be aware the food portions are a lot larger than you would typically expect. The primary chef is from Oaxaca.

Enormous club with 7 floors. However, despite its popularity this club is usually not worth visiting. The owner has a policy to try to limit the number of foreigners in the club so if you are from anywhere except Spain, you will likely…

Branch of the popular nationwide chain that offers 100 different montaditos (small sandwiches). Great place to go for a cheap drink and bite to eat. Further branches are at Calle de la Montera, 34 (near metro Gran Vía) and Plaza de las…
Very solid local option for small dishes/tapas. Recommended are chorizo, pig ears, tortilla with chorizo (omelette with chorizo), morcilla, sepia a la plancha. Casual non pretentious place.
Fantastic little stop for tapas. A very cozy place with good tapas and they always treat you very well. With a funny decoration.
Good taqueria. The tacos are amazing. The quesadillas and tortas are also worth it. The queue seems super long, but it moves fast.
Small little cantine with excellent and satisfying authentic Spanish food. You have to queue, but it's quite fluid and it's worth it.
Lively market that has not been completely swamped by tourism. Wide range of food & drink available. (including Vegan)
This is a good place to drop by on a hot afternoon to enjoy a cold beer and some Andalusian tapas. Sample the sausages and cheeses.

A Madrid landmark in operation for over 100 years, this bar attracts a standing room only crowd on the weekends. They mainly serve shrimp-based tapas dishes so if you're not into shellfish it may be advisable to steer clear. Order a…
For something different, try this great Peruvian restaurant a short walk from Sol. Be sure to order some of their ceviche and try the Pisco Sour cocktail.
All-vegan restaurant that doesn't compromise on flavor, a good place to try vegan versions of Spanish tortilla and croquetas.
Café by day, live jazz music at night.
Famous for its pastries. Peaceful upstairs room where you can linger undisturbed over your café con leche and napolitana de chocolate (chocolate croissant).
Slightly scruffy cafe draws an avante garde crowd at night.

eat.n: La Pecera del Círculo de Bellas Artes
eat.b: A soaring hall on the ground floor of Madrid's art center combines atmosphere, excellent food and good coffee at reasonable prices. A wonderful place for lunch not far from Madrid's shopping or museums.

Voted the Best European Bar 2004 by MTV-Campari. Extensive cocktail list. Claims to have served drinks to many famous celebrities, including, Ava Gardner, Frank Sinatra, Lana Turner, Gary Cooper, Orson Wells, Yul Brynner and Ernest…
An Irish bar in the centre of Madrid near Puerta del Sol. The bar has televisions and is one of the places where sport can be seen.
Discopub in the core of Barrio de las Letras. Great place with excellent prices but a good quality. The bar includes nice music, a DJ, and a moderately large dance floor.

eat.a: Calle de Manuel Fernández y González, 7
eat.b: Opened in 1856, this Madrid institution is known for its old-world charm and its creative takes on tapas and cocktails. José Rizal, the Philippines' national hero, was a regular patron, with a plaque hanging above the door in his honor.
Interesting mixture of unusual local and foreign beers.
Popular with the 20-30 age group. Plays a mix of 70s, funk, and bossanova sounds. No dress code, but people do tend to look cool.

eat.a: Plaza de Callao, 1 (in Gran Via street)
eat.b: Popular Commercial House club with a mixed young straight/gay crowd.
Powerful Techno/House club popular within the younger crowd.

Streetfood market on Fuencarral street, right in the middle of the Malasaña-Chueca area. 15 different stalls offer arepas (cornmeal griddlecake), brochetas (skewer), tacos, tapas, ham, meats, wine, beer etc. Between late-May and…
The very best huevos rotos ('broken eggs') and croquetas. Cheap, beautiful and delicious! The chicken-adorned tiled front dates from the 19th century.
THE place for serious hamburgers. Americans will feel at home!

eat.a: Calle Corredera Alta de San Pablo 8
eat.b: Taperia with lunch room out the back. Reviews mixed about the tapas but great place for lunch; they do a great Cocido Madrileño and the house wine is more than acceptable (although served somewhat cold).
All plant based, mainly burger menu but with a few other items. If you like beer, their own craft bottled beers are good. English menu available.

This dark, cave-like Moroccan restaurant has some of the best North African food in the city. The seating is at low Moroccan-style tables and the calm, mellow atmosphere makes you feel like you're far from the bustling center of Chueca.
Nice designer restaurant popular within the 20s-30s crowd. Good music, cool people, even better food and cocktails. The kitchen opens in the afternoon.
This is a small, usually crowded, friendly Mexican restaurant with good food and drinks at reasonable prices. Sample some of their tacos and super-cheesy chilaquiles.
Recommended for paella if a more authentic experience is sought.
Beautifully-decorated with a tranquil atmosphere, the food is reasonable and offers a pleasant departure from Spanish fare, if so desired.

Probably the most well-known tapas bar in Madrid, a must do. Don't get frightened by how crowded the bar is and go in anyway. This is one of the most lively places in the city! Get beers, big glasses of wine or un mini de mojito and get…
Opened in the 1880s, this is the oldest cafe in Madrid, and has been run by the same family since the early 1900s. There's a modern internet café upstairs, but the downstairs remains traditional.
Long-standing confectionery (established 1914), offering excellent tartlets that are not only delicious but also look picture-perfect. They are also sold to take away.
A historic literary cafe. The outdoor terraza is nice in the summer.

eat.pr: Café: €14-15 (midweek set menu), €19-20 (weekend set menu); Restaurant: set menu
eat.b: Opened in 1978, but looks much older. Has two divisions: a more casual café and a restaurant. Good food and very crowded during lunchtime.

Café, crêperie (place making crepes), sweets and very friendly staff – a good place for lovers of desserts and the sweet.

Very cool chill out bar decorated with deep colours in a Moroccan style. Dark and inviting. The seating includes cushions on the floor, traditional tables and chairs, or if you’re lucky, grab the four poster bed at the back.
A swingin' bar where you can twist the night away with local hipsters.
Cosy craft beer bar with their own range of beers
Cool electronic sounds for 20s-30s.
Smallish venue, starts the night with live jazz, later on morphs into relaxed night club. Not cheap (once inside, beer still €5.50, mixed drink €8.50), so attracts older crowd than others nearby.
A family-run restaurant operating since 1870 and serving traditional Madrileño cuisine. Reservations can be made online.
Specializing in chocolate con churros, this Madrid fixture is the perfect place to top off a night on the town. Also offers the usual assortment of coffees and teas.
Serves typical Madrid cuisine.

Pricey but worth it. The Spanish Royal family sometimes entertain guests here and you may run into a few sports figures and movie stars. You should definitely book ahead on the weekends, and reservations are recommended even for the…

Opened in 1725, Botín is listed in the Guinness Book of Records as the oldest operating restaurant in the world. Once a favourite of Ernest Hemingway, the menu still delights with specialities including cochinillo (roast suckling pig)…

Sherry-tasting available in 8 languages. Commentary by knowledgeable oenologists explaining the details of the history, elaboration methods and tasting notes for each of the wines, while inviting guests to combine them with tapas served…
Overlooks the Plaza Oriente and faces Palacio Real. Outdoor tables in summer, cozy indoor rooms in the cold months. Basement banquet room with a glass floor over ancient remains. Excellent food.
Specializes in delicious ‘tostas’ (small pieces of toast with different toppings) and avocado (aguacate), along with cañas (small beers).
Well known across Europe. Attracts at multi-national crowd. Popular with tourists as well as locals. It plays a mix of popular dance music. Every Thursday there is a Students Party.
A third branch of the popular establishment.

A great place for tapas, they offer a large menu, reasonable prices and excellent quality food. The solomillo al foie is excellent and the desserts come highly-recommended as well. Very crowded on Friday and Saturday nights.

An excellent tapas bar and restaurant. A nice place to enjoy Spanish food and lifestyle without spending too much. Located in a business park in the far-east of the city, it's far from being a tourist trap and you can enjoy good food…

eat.h: Mon-Sat 13:00-16:00 20:00-24:00; closed the month of Aug
eat.b: A Madrid institution for decades, Trainera is an excellent but somewhat pricey restaurant serving strictly seafood dishes. They have a great wine selection and the waiters can recommend different vintages that will complement the food.…
Best paella in Madrid, but only if you bring more than two people by order of the proprietor. Frequented mainly by locals, prepare to be stared at by the wait staff if you are from out of town.
Seafood.
Arguably the best seafood in Madrid.
Craft beers & good selection of Belgian & German Beers
